title: FACT CHECK: No death penalty for Filipina arrested in Hong Kong for drug trafficking
summary: The death penalty has long been abolished in Hong Kong

blocks.text: Claim: The Filipino woman arrested in Hong Kong for illegal possession of drugs may be executed by hanging.
Why we fact-checked this: The claim was made in a post by the Facebook page “JIL Review TV” on November 8. The page currently has over 130,000 followers.
As of writing, it has received 3,800 reactions, 1,600 comments, and 150 shares.
Text on the post reads, “BREAKING: Posibleng bibitayin ang Pinay na nahulihan ng cocaine sa HK.”
(BREAKING: Filipina caught with cocaine in Hong Kong faces possible execution.)

The facts: Capital punishment, whether by hanging or any other method of execution, is not legal in Hong Kong. The death penalty was formally abolished through the Crimes (Amendment) Ordinance in 1993, with the last execution carried out in November 1966.

The false claim stemmed from reports that a 22-year-old Filipino woman arriving from Phnom Penh was arrested in Hong Kong on October 31 for suspected drug trafficking. During customs clearance protocols, about 6 kilograms of suspected cocaine with an estimated market value of about HK$3.6 million was found in her suitcase.
Under Hong Kong’s Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, drug trafficking carries a maximum penalty upon conviction of a fine of $5 million and life imprisonment.

The Filipina was charged with one count of trafficking in a dangerous drug and her case was set to be brought to the West Kowloon Magistrates’ Court on November 2. As of writing, there are no updates on the court’s ruling on her case.

Recent drug busts: The case follows other recently reported drug trafficking cases. On October 1, a major drug bust happened in Laos, where a private jet carrying 521 kilos of suspected shabu worth P3.5 billion was intercepted. It was reportedly bound for Manila. (READ: Inside story: Politician behind 521-kilo shabu shipment bound for Manila)
On October 17, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said 11 persons of interest are linked to the shipment, including a former Bangsamoro Parliament member.
A Filipino, Fahad Mulok Dibarosan, was arrested in the Laos drug bust. Authorities said they will appeal to commute a possible death sentence for the arrested Filipino.

In a separate incident, Thai authorities intercepted about 1,178 kilograms of suspected shabu aboard a fishing vessel in the Gulf of Thailand in early October. Authorities later said there was no evidence indicating that the shipment was bound for the Philippines. – Lourence Angelo Marcellana/Rappler.com
